source.title: Sparse Double Descent: Where Network Pruning Aggravates Overfitting
source.authors: Zhengqi He; Zeke Xie; Quanzhi Zhu; Zeng-Chang Qin

record.tranche_reason: Reports that pruning can worsen overfitting at moderate sparsities, then relieve it at higher sparsities under label noise; this refines the generalization story but does not test a listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative train/test accuracy patterns and learning-distance curves; cited findings from other work are not included as rows. Figure-only numerical values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests pruning-induced changes in generalization, which none of V1–V8 names. It varies sparsity rather than width, and its learning-distance and indirect flatness analyses do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or ranking of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report sparse double descent under label noise and propose learning distance as a partial explanation. Their conclusions also include indirect evidence against a flat-basin explanation and cases where randomly reinitialized sparse networks outperform lottery-ticket initializations.
record.recipe_differences: Studies iterative weight pruning and retraining on synthetic noisy-label datasets, not the original claim's random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported curves vary with dataset, noise rate and type, pruning strategy, retraining method, and sparsity. Heavier label noise shifts the critical and sweet phases; without label noise, the pattern is rarely evident in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Under label noise, increasing sparsity can worsen final test accuracy, then improve it, then degrade it at extreme sparsity. The pattern is rarely evident without label noise and is less pronounced when selecting the best epoch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterative pruning can produce sparse double descent, depending on label noise and the epoch used to evaluate performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Distance from initialization partly tracks sparse double descent on MNIST, but the critical-phase comparison on CIFAR-100 and the collapsed phase qualify that relationship.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 learning distance is a conditional correlate of generalization across sparsities.

fits_no_version.finding: Restoring pruned weights and continuing training can cause severe overfitting; filter-normalized loss slices show sharper final re-dense solutions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of highly sparse solutions need not be explained by remaining in a flat basin after sparsity constraints are removed.

record.problems: Most reported accuracy and distance values are shown in figures without numeric tables; the text describes qualitative trends. The learning-distance relation is correlational, and the authors note a CIFAR case that does not show the MNIST-style distance peak.
record.rows_left_out: No additional text-reported outcomes on the listed versions were found. Other figure-only sweeps across pruning strategies, noise rates, retraining methods, model families, and sparsities are not individually extracted; the paper's text summarizes these as robust qualitative patterns without giving per-setting numeric outcomes.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fully random-label training, including held-out performance under each.
Widening networks beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on matched image tasks, including the role of local connectivity and initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error and its dependence on training-set size, strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No version-level verdict is warranted. Partial label corruption does not supply V1's matched random-label experiment, and the flatness discussion does not establish a test of V7's specified measure.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels.
Varies sparsity by pruning, not width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional networks with fully connected networks on image generalization.
Uses SGD; does not compare adaptive optimizers.
Does not vary batch size to test a large-batch penalty.
Measures learning distance and discusses minima flatness, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures as specified.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: LeNet-300-100
rows.size_stated: 300 units in the first layer and 100 units in the second hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Increasing model sparsity by iterative magnitude-based pruning and lottery-ticket rewinding; measures train and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy across sparsity; authors describe test accuracy as first decreasing, then increasing, then decreasing again as sparsity grows.
rows.baseline: Dense model (0% sparsity; numerical accuracy not stated in text).
rows.value: Figure 1 plots sparsities 0, 58.9, 83.2, 93.1, 97.2, 98.8, and 99.5%; numerical accuracies are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation over five runs are plotted; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: Text says the pattern is observed for LeNet-300-100 on MNIST with noisy labels; exact plotted accuracies are not transcribed.
rows.check: The qualitative sparse double-descent finding is supported, but pruning a fixed architecture does not test V2's widening claim. This state concerns the listed versions.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Increasing model sparsity by iterative magnitude-based pruning and lottery-ticket rewinding; measures train and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Train and test accuracy across sparsity; authors describe test accuracy as first decreasing, then increasing, then decreasing again as sparsity grows.
rows.baseline: Dense model (0% sparsity; numerical accuracy not stated in text).
rows.value: Figure 1 plots sparsities 0, 58.9, 83.2, 93.1, 97.2, 98.8, and 99.5%; numerical accuracies are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation over three runs are plotted; numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The authors state the sparse double descent is observed for ResNet-18 on CIFAR; Figure 1's middle panel is CIFAR-10.
rows.check: The reported accuracy pattern concerns sparsity under partially corrupted labels, not widening or a fully random-label versus natural-label comparison.

rows.subject: LeNet-300-100
rows.size_stated: 300 units in the first layer and 100 units in the second hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Measures L2 distance from original dense initialization to learned parameters across sparsity and compares its curve with test accuracy.
rows.measure: L2 learning distance and test accuracy as functions of sparsity; text says their changing curves coincide and the turning point usually aligns with a learning-distance peak.
rows.value: Figure-only curves; text reports a correlation between learning distance and test accuracy.
rows.note: A correlational measure, not the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7; the authors qualify its informativeness in the collapsed phase.
rows.check: L2 distance from initialization is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. The text describes greater distance accompanying worse accuracy in the critical phase; the curves should not be interpreted as positively correlated throughout.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measures L2 distance from original dense initialization to learned parameters across sparsity and compares its curve with test accuracy.
rows.measure: L2 learning distance and test accuracy as functions of sparsity; text notes the critical-phase model has lower test accuracy than the dense model without a higher critical learning distance.
rows.baseline: Dense model (reference comparison; numerical values not stated).
rows.value: Figure-only curves; text states the critical learning distance is not higher than the dense model's.
rows.note: The authors identify this as differing from MNIST and say distance may be affected by scale invariance and batch normalization.
rows.check: This is a qualification of the learning-distance hypothesis, not evidence about V7's sharpness measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
